newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, US sign agreements for $416 mln in grants.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, US sign agreements for $416 mln in grants.

text.p: Egypt and the United States signed on Tuesday 10 grant agreements worth a total $416.1 million.

The package, dominated by a $200 million grant to support what the United States called sector policy reform, amounts to almost half the annual U.S. civilian aid to Egypt currently running at about $900 million a year.

"These agreements embody important aspects of the growing collaboration that exists between the United States and Egypt to advance Egypt's participation in the global economy," U.S. ambassador Edward Walker told the signing ceremony.

"They provide support for economic policy reforms to increase private sector productivity and exports, enhance competitive markets, protect the environment and promote privatisation," added an embassy press release.
Walker and U.S. Agency for International Development director John Westley signed for the United States, Economy and International Cooperation Minister Nawal el-Tatawi for Egypt.
The second largest grant, for $61.1 million, is designed to transform the state-owned telecommunications company ARENTO into an autonomous and self-sustaining entity.
The United States also gives Egypt about $1.2 billion a year in military aid, mainly to buy weapons.
